solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Economiser? Not half!

indicators.note: not half tells us to drop the first five of the ten letters of the clue's opening word, keeping only the back half

explanation.surface: A reply to someone asking whether a person is thrifty: not half, meaning very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', but here it is a literal instruction: lose half the word. The second half of the ten-letter word left behind is itself a thrifty person.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money, an extreme kind of saver, and the letters left after the cut are exactly that word.

clue.text: Puccini's seamstress repeated note

indicators.note: repeated says the musical syllable is written down twice

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Puccini's seamstress sings the same note twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimì, the frail embroiderer, is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème.

clue.text: Colin fiddled with his PC, installing one?

definitions.text: Colin fiddled with his PC, installing one?

indicators.note: installing means fitting inside, so the letter is placed within the shuffled letters
fiddled with means tampered, so the name and the following words are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Colin tinkered with his computer and fitted a new component.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-&lit: the whole clue describes fitting this microchip into a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: An integrated circuit on a wafer of the element used in semiconductors is the part one would fit into a computer.

clue.text: Girl spots wrapping for vegetable

indicators.note: wrapping means wrapped around, so the spots word encloses the name

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A girl notices blemishes on the wrapping of a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: This peppery red root is a common salad vegetable.

clue.text: Obsessive is, say, back on drug — this one?

definitions.text: Obsessive is, say, back on drug — this one?

indicators.note: on places the earlier pieces before the final letter, as if resting on it

parts.note: anal is informal for fussily obsessive, short for anal-retentive

indicators.note: back says the two little words before it are read from right to left

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a fussy, compulsive person is back on a certain drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS + EG into GESI. The whole clue then doubles as a hint: the drug in question is one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is a drug, so the semi-cryptic reading invites the solver to name a pain-relieving medicine.

clue.text: What's run over by learner in windy Lima road?

indicators.note: in places the learner's letter inside the rearranged letters
a windy road twists, so the letters of the place and road are wound into a new order

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: Something is hit by a learner driver on a winding road near Lima.
explanation.walkthrough: These armoured animals are famous as roadkill in the Americas, hence 'What's run over'.
explanation.definitionFit: This armoured mammal often ends up as roadkill on American roads, so it is typically the thing hit by cars.

clue.text: Chilean desert borders them

indicators.note: borders means lies on either side of, so the two words surround the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A desert in Chile lies on the edge of a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the letters sit across 'Chilean desert', and the Atacama desert really does border the range.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South American mountain chain runs down Chile's eastern edge beside the Atacama desert.

clue.text: Fuel tank lacks ordinary means of tapping it

indicators.note: lacks means is without, so the letter for ordinary is dropped

parts.note: a gasometer is a large tank storing gas, a fuel
O is short for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A fuel tank has no ordinary way to draw fuel from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers to the fuel: the device measures how much gas a home draws from the supply. The blogger read the tank as METEOR, but commenters favoured GASOMETER less O.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic meter records how much gas is drawn from the mains, so it is how the supply is tapped and charged.

clue.text: What to do in Zürs, Kitzbühel etc

definitions.text: What to do in Zürs, Kitzbühel etc

indicators.note: in says the letters are found inside the two resort names

explanation.surface: What visitors do at Austrian resorts such as Zürs and Kitzbühel.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the letters span the end of one resort name and the start of the next, and both are Austrian winter sports resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Zürs and Kitzbühel are Alpine winter resorts where people go to slide down snow slopes.

clue.text: They bring down 100 game birds, taking pressure off

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: taking ... off means removing, so the letter for pressure comes out of the birds
off completes the instruction to remove that letter from the birds

parts.note: partridges are shot as game birds
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Shooters bag a hundred game birds, which relieves the pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring down' suggests the hunters; it is the ammunition that brings birds down.
explanation.definitionFit: Shotgun shells are what actually bring down birds on a shoot, so they are the things that bring down game.

clue.text: Retainer's mother nursing sick daughter

definitions.note: read as 'retainer is', the apostrophe s acting as a link

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the parent word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: mam is a dialect word for mum
ill means sick
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A family servant's mother is caring for her ailing daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retainer' suggests a household servant, but here it means something that holds water back.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill dam holds back a stream to make a millpond, so it retains water.

clue.text: He sleeps rough, clutching current papers

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the sleeper's word grips the other letter inside it

parts.note: a dosser is British slang for someone who sleeps on the streets
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A homeless man sleeping outdoors holds on to today's newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' looks like newspapers to keep him warm; it is a file of documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A file of documents gathered on one subject or person is a set of papers.

clue.text: Islamic judge securing quiet poet's source of notes

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly, so the judge's title wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a cadi (or qadi) is a judge in a Muslim court
sh is the call for silence
Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: A Muslim judge quietly guards a poet's source of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' hints at poetry or music; it means banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine is where banknotes come from, so it is a source of paper money.

clue.text: Cover small donkey spied touring Cork regularly

parts.note: S is short for small, as in clothing sizes
moke is British slang for a donkey

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the spied word goes round the chosen letters

parts.note: seen means spied or noticed

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the Irish county name

explanation.surface: A small donkey is seen on a tour of County Cork, under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meant to hide one's real activities is a cover, as with a pretence or a cloud of smoke.

clue.text: Reword speech of soldier on stage carrying spear finally

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the soldier above the stage piece

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the stage word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a phase is a stage in a process

indicators.note: finally means taking the final letter of the weapon word

explanation.surface: An actor playing a soldier carries a spear on stage as he speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate someone's speech or writing in different words is to reword it.

clue.text: It worries adolescent, except oldest maybe

indicators.note: except tells us to take away the letters of the following word from the clue word before it
maybe signals that the remaining letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something troubles a teenager, apart from the eldest child perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of OLDEST from ADOLESCENT and A, C, E, N remain; 'maybe' rearranges those. The definition leans on the clue's 'adolescent', so the whole reads as a description too.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots on the face are a classic teenage worry, which makes this skin complaint something that troubles young people.

clue.text: All he does is bankrupt property

indicators.note: bankrupt suggests something broken up, so the words before it are reshuffled

explanation.surface: All this man does is go bust over a property deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Land or a flat held on a lease for a fixed term is a form of property tenure.

clue.text: Hard-working Saudis everywhere love the FT

indicators.note: everywhere suggests scattered all over, so the nationality's letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
the newspaper referring to itself as 'we' would say us

explanation.surface: Saudi readers all over the world adore the Financial Times for its diligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the FT' is the setter's own paper speaking of itself, so it stands for 'us'.
explanation.definitionFit: Assiduous describes someone diligent and persevering, a close synonym for hard-working.

clue.text: Teacher mounted offensive, engaging censor once

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the turned word holds the Roman name
mounted, in a down clue, means going upwards, so the word for offensive is read bottom to top

parts.note: rude means offensive
Cato the Elder was a famous censor in ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A teacher launched an attack, involving a past censor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns the rude word upwards in this down clue. Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor, policing public morals, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Educator is a formal word for someone who teaches, a direct synonym.

clue.text: An American's taken over spa with no water

indicators.note: taken over means swallowed up, so the opening pieces close around the spa word

parts.note: US is short for American; the 's is 'has'
a hydro is a hydropathic hotel or spa

explanation.surface: An American has bought a spa which has no water.
explanation.walkthrough: A hydro is a British term for a hydropathic hotel, a spa resort offering water cures; the joke is that the answer means waterless.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists call a substance anhydrous when it contains no water, from the Greek for 'waterless'.

clue.text: Evergreen shrub among the begonias

indicators.note: among says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An evergreen bush planted with the begonias in a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe is a genus of evergreen garden shrubs from New Zealand, named after the Greek goddess of youth.

clue.text: Lead row across river

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the quarrel word stretches over the river

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Take charge as a row breaks out on the far side of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a piece of advance information, the sense of 'lead' as in a clue for detectives.

clue.text: Phony chair doc arranged for him?

definitions.text: Phony chair doc arranged for him?

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fake doctor's chair has been set up for a patient who imagines his illnesses.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a sham consulting room is what someone with imaginary ailments deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone convinced they are ill without cause is a hypochondriac, the natural patient of a fake doctor.

clue.text: Start filming

definitions.meaning: a beginning, as of an illness or season
..., where a film is being shot

explanation.definitionFit: Onset is a beginning, and split in two it reads 'on set', where actors work while filming.

clue.text: Perhaps 8 25s?

parts.note: 25 down is the binary unit, and eight of those binary units make up the computing unit asked for

explanation.surface: A puzzle reference: maybe eight of the 25 down answers.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing eight binary digits form one standard unit of data storage.

clue.text: Bush was popular but useless to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A judgment on President Bush: popular, but useless in part.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Bush was' fails the swap test; 'Bush' alone is the shrub and 'was' is a link word. The surface invites a reading about George Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree is a bushy evergreen shrub of the genus with this name.

clue.text: Sank teeth into fragment

definitions.meaning: past tense of the verb meaning to use one's teeth on something

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of the verb for chomping and also means a small piece.

clue.text: Outcome of smashing plates in one orgy possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way, so the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Broken crockery is what happens at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plates' suggests plate-smashing at a party; it means tectonic plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountain-building occurs when the Earth's crustal plates collide, so it results from plates crashing together.

clue.text: Tube complaint? It is put on record

indicators.note: put on places the opening words after the record word, attached to its end

parts.note: to enter is to record, as in a ledger

explanation.surface: A grievance about London's Underground is formally logged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground; it is the intestine.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the intestine is an illness of the gut, a tube in the body.

clue.text: Old fellow avoids wrong dealer

indicators.note: avoids means keeps away from, so those two letters are left out of the next word

parts.note: an offence is a wrong or crime

explanation.surface: An elderly man keeps clear of a crooked trader.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is slang for a dealer in stolen goods, which fits the criminal surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a receiver who trades in stolen goods is called this, so he is a kind of dealer.
